finding.claim: SQL injection (class: injection) in /search. The unauthenticated `q` query parameter is interpolated directly into an f-string SQL query, so an attacker can break out of the LIKE literal. They can use UNION SELECT to read any table or column in shop.db, including data not exposed by the product endpoints. Impact is arbitrary read of the database. Stacked writes are not possible because sqlite3 `execute` runs a single statement.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: Route handler /search, no auth decorator or middleware
term taken from request.args with no validation
term formatted into SQL string via f-string and executed
Query results returned as JSON, so UNION-based injection output is exfiltrated directly

finding.guards_checked: No parameterization, escaping, allowlist, length limit or authentication on this path. The sibling handlers at app.py:18 and app.py:25 use `?` placeholders, so this is the only unparameterized query. /product/<int:pid> is also constrained to int by Flask's route converter. The app has no auth or tenant model, so I did not report missing authz on /by-owner or /product as a separate finding.

verdict.reason: app.py:11 reads `q` from request.args and app.py:12 interpolates it into an f-string SQL query with no parameterization, auth, or validation, and app.py:13 returns the rows as JSON, so a UNION injection is exfiltrated directly.
